source: Coordinator's brief for 8.0.0-beta.6, 2026-11-21 (the properties review, items 22, 23 and 26; memory by heap share); RFC 0006 §9.3
statement: Every share of the heap CoSec takes is in one table (`HeapBudget`, `cosec-runtime`): the revocation tables 1/8, the verified-token cache 1/16, the BEST_EFFORT decision listeners' queues 1/64, the change listeners' queues 1/32, and the memberships 1/64 (`MEM-5`), and a quarter for the snapshot documents, from which their families' bounds are derived (`SNP-24`); where the control plane runs, that quarter is held a third each by the pipeline's snapshot source, the control plane's own, and the one document cache simulate, explain, analyze and the lock-out check share (DR1-F-5), so no cache of the control plane takes a share beside the table. Together they take at most half of `Runtime.maxMemory()`. Each share is chosen so that at the production overlay's 2 GiB heap its bound is not below the count it replaced, and a smaller heap gets less, never nothing. No property sets any of them: `cosec.observability.listener.queue-capacity`, `cosec.authentication.token-cache.max-entries` and `cosec.authentication.revocation.cache.maximum-size` fail startup as keys CoSec does not read, saying what replaced them. The starter says once at startup what each budget came to and from what. Two bounds are still counts and take no share, since no anonymous caller can grow either (8.1 makes them shares): the unknown principals remembered locally, 10,000 (`UnknownPrincipals`, one id and a time each, under 200 bytes: about 2 MB; principals come from verified credentials only), and the compiled shadow candidates, 1,024 (`CachingCandidateSource`, one compiled candidate document each, as large as the document it compiles; candidates come only from changes the control plane staged).
